attempts.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset: exactly 12 true consecutive animation drawings of Patrick Star in one transparent sprite atlas, 4 columns by 3 rows, reading left-to-right and top-to-bottom, overall 4:3 sheet, equal square cells.
Input reference role: borrow ONLY the cartoon Patrick's upside-down waffle-cone hat, usual green shorts with purple flower shapes, and small hand-held ice cream from the phone-case artwork on the right of the reference screenshot. It is NOT approval to reproduce the screenshot, branding, product, typography or background.
Transform this outfit idea into clean original-cartoon-style 2D cel animation. Patrick has his familiar pink starfish head/body, broad belly, short rounded feet and natural cartoon anatomy, not tall and skinny, not realistic, not a plush toy. Black crisp outlines and simple cel colors. Pure white eye whites and black pupils. Eyelids always warm coral pink matching skin, no purple/grey/lavender eye skin.
Wear one small tan upside-down waffle cone as a hat, firmly on head throughout. Same one small ice-cream cone held in his screen-right hand throughout, pale pistachio-green scoop with a simple cream swirl. Other hand relaxed or briefly on belly. No switching hands or duplicate cones.
Narrative, twelve genuinely different poses:
1 neutral, cone held near chest to screen-right, looking forward.
2 pupils slide toward the treat, one brow lifts.
3 sly sideways glance, tiny anticipatory smile; cone starts moving inward.
4 elbow bends and cone moves closer to the face; head only leans a little.
5 opens mouth slightly, tongue just begins to extend toward scoop.
6 tongue lightly touches the near edge of scoop, same hand and cone clearly visible.
7 tongue retracts, treat moves a little away; leave a tiny smooth lick groove on scoop that remains in later frames.
8 eyes gently close with a pleased smile, cone still by chest, same size with lick groove retained.
9 satisfied small smile, relaxed shoulders, one brief hand on belly if anatomically clear.
10 eyes suddenly open, tries to look innocent, lowering cone slightly.
11 regains a straight-faced serious expression, ice cream at original chest position.
12 calm innocent forward gaze, same stance/body proportions as frame1, cone with the small lick mark still present.
This is real facial and arm animation, not copies translated or the whole character rocked/scaled. Tongue and mouth changes must be coherent and small. Hat never becomes the hand-held cone. One scoop, no magically restored consumed food, no extra hands/fingers.
Camera locked frontal, whole character drawn at one consistent scale and body volume across all12. Same local foot baseline. Natural small expression/pose projection allowed, but no changing head/body proportion or per-frame fitting. Cap, head, arms, treat and both bare feet fully contained inside each cell. Leave ample top/bottom transparent safety margin and wide transparent gutters. No frame text, labels, border, floor, shadow, glow or gradients.
Genuine transparent RGBA background, not a painted checkerboard.

Use case: illustration-story.
Asset: one clean 2D cel-animation atlas of Patrick Star playing a careful tennis forehand, exactly 12 distinct consecutive full-body frames arranged in 4 columns and 3 rows, left-to-right top-to-bottom. Overall landscape 4:3 sheet, equal square cells. Genuine transparent RGBA background.
Character and outfit: Patrick Star in his recognizable original cartoon design: warm pink starfish, broad round belly, naturally compact body and short rounded feet, not a tall thin human and not a plush doll. Cream short-sleeve tennis polo with teal collar and sleeve trim, teal sports shorts with a small cream stripe, cream-and-teal headband, bare pink feet clearly visible. Clean black outline and flat cel colors. Pure white sclera, black pupils; eyelids warm coral-pink matching skin, never purple/lavender/grey. His expression is serious and focused, not a smile in every frame.
One appropriately small teal-and-cream tennis racket held by the same anatomical right hand throughout (starts at screen-right in the front view). The hand continuously grips the same handle, racket never changes hand or duplicates. Other arm balances the action.
Action,12 newly drawn poses:
1. Frontal ready stance, racket low at screen-right, focused forward gaze.
2. Slight athletic knee bend and elbows prepare; keep the same body volume.
3. Small torso turn toward his racket side and racket begins the backswing, eye gaze follows approaching ball.
4. Backswing complete, racket angled back, one small yellow ball approaches from screen-left.
5. Forehand swings forward, ball now immediately before the racket face; maintain one wrist/handle connection.
6. Clear contact moment at waist height, racket face hits that one yellow ball; no duplicate or ghost ball.
7. Follow-through begins across the front of the torso toward screen-left; ball travels away toward screen-right with no blur trail.
8. Racket continues the follow-through across chest, supporting hand stays separate, brows concentrated. Ball is now outside the frame, not another ball.
9. Shoulders relax a little, racket lowers from follow-through, eyes track the departing shot.
10. Same hand brings racket back toward the original screen-right side.
11. Racket and arms settle into ready stance.
12. Exact same physical neutral body proportions, camera scale and foot baseline as frame1, serious forward gaze, racket low at screen-right.
Real articulated poses: shoulder, elbow, wrist/racket and face change with a coherent forehand. No shifting a single whole image, no repeated frames, no extra arms, fingers or rackets. Keep every racket rim and handle fully visible. Do not hide the grip with arbitrary effects. No words, logos, action symbols, motion blur or swoosh lines.
Camera stays locked at the same front viewpoint; a modest torso twist and foot pivot show real sport movement, but body/head dimensions and drawing scale must stay consistent. Do not grow or shrink Patrick to fit each cell. Keep a stable common ground reference with feet supported; don't confuse natural knee bend with resizing. Use wide transparent gutters and generous head, feet and sideways racket safety margins. Full headband, head, arms, racket, shorts and both feet fit completely inside every cell. No court, net, floor, cast shadow, halo, vignette, border, labels or numbers.
